report_review.scope_depth_review: Within the assigned 1,200–1,800-word budget and eight-URL ceiling. It traces two concrete contracts: Mamba's typed non-final chunk-state writes with an FP32 carry/final state, and FLA's backward rematerialization of chunk intermediates. The comparison identifies when storage traffic or retained training activations may matter, includes counterexamples and a bounded future evaluation, and explicitly withholds B570 speed, model-quality, and adoption claims.
report_review.novelty_and_redundancy: The source-level state-passing/materialization graph is incremental to R759's global scan/work-map scheduling and R782's general framework dtype/state contracts. R786's graph fan-in scope is unrelated. R773 already covers chunk-size, workspace, shared-state, and tail tradeoffs; R820's technical question remains distinct, but its proposed sequence/chunk-size/tail sweep overlaps R773's proposed 4K/8K/16K comparison. Any future experiment should reuse an already selected chunk/tail control and isolate state dtype/recomputation, rather than repeat a separate chunk-size study.

source_attribution.assessment: The report pins Mamba and FLA source paths to immutable commits, links each repository license, and identifies the Intel SYCL matrix-extension file. Direct read-only checks of the pinned sources confirmed the described Mamba FP32 carry and typed materialization, FLA backward rematerialization and typed h allocation, and the Intel API's experimental subgroup scope and device-specific type/shape queries. These are source contracts, not performance measurements.
source_attribution.limitations: The Intel documentation URL follows the mutable sycl branch; the report gives its retrieval date but no immutable revision. None of the sources establishes an Arc B570 runtime tuple, a winning storage format, task-level numerical acceptance, or a Strata performance result. No third-party source text was copied.

unsupported_or_unverified_inferences.claim: The report says BMG-family combinations in the cited Intel specification provide a route to investigate matrix support.
unsupported_or_unverified_inferences.finding: The linked specification does not identify BMG; it documents an experimental subgroup API and requires querying each device's supported type/shape combinations. Remove the BMG-specific attribution or state it only as a hypothesis to check against the exact B570 runtime.

unsupported_or_unverified_inferences.claim: Scalar affine state passing is likely a better first port than using matrix hardware; Strata's GDN geometry and chunk schedule differ from the cited implementations.
unsupported_or_unverified_inferences.finding: These are reasonable design hypotheses, not source-measured conclusions. Mark the first explicitly as inference and attach a local source path/revision to the Strata geometry statement if it is reused.

report_review.provenance_limit: Pinned upstream source was checked read-only for the stated contracts and licenses. No Strata implementation source, B570 runtime, performance result, numerical result, or model acceptance was independently checked. Research remains decision context only.

next_research_scopes.title: Error growth and correction policies for low-precision recurrent checkpoints
next_research_scopes.finite_question: If a Main-owned natural-input recurrence comparison localizes unacceptable error to a 16-bit chunk-state write, what do numerical-analysis and implemented GPU/ASIC sources establish about error growth under contractive versus near-unit affine transitions, and which two concrete correction policies (for example, block rescaling versus compensated state storage) reduce it? Record exact arithmetic/storage cadence, tested dynamic range and sequence length, reported accuracy and cost, and counterexamples. Do not repeat R820's fixed-precision materialization-versus-recomputation graph or R773's chunk-size/tail sweep.
next_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use primary papers and implementation/documentation sources for two concrete correction policies; distinguish analytic bounds from measured results and hardware-specific timing. Do not claim B570 applicability, propose source reuse, or recommend a Strata precision change.
next_research_scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 words; at most six substantive primary sources with exact URLs, one policy/contract comparison table, and explicit evidence limits.

Current supplied work is GEMM qualification and source/knowledge research; it does not provide that recurrence error evidence.
